implementation_summary: Implemented and independently reviewed bounded RSS 2.0 and Atom ingestion through the shared fetcher and normalization pipeline with transactional cursor persistence and strict namespace handling.

files_changed.change: Added bounded RSS/Atom parsing, strict supported namespaces, date/encoding/relative-link mappings, diagnostics, conditional validators, and exact byte-limit handling.
Added parser, mapping, namespace-collision, encoding, malformed, exact-limit, over-limit, and conditional-fetch tests.
Added production orchestration that transactionally owns normalized article writes and source cursor advancement.
Added consumed RSS, Atom, namespace, and malformed-document fixtures with coverage documentation.
Added controlled-server and temporary-SQLite cursor, rollback, 304, permission, and ingestion lifecycle proof.

verification.output: Parsing, namespaces, limits, conditional requests, rollback, cursor, and permission tests passed repeatedly.
All Go packages passed race and vet checks.
Full Go, repository, frontend, browser, and PWA verification passed.
Feed, ingestion, and integration packages compiled for Windows.

verification.output: Diff, scope, and secrecy checks passed.

proof.summary: Normalization, article, and source-save failures roll back article/cursor state; 304 performs zero article calls and transactionally persists validators.
RSS, Atom, Dublin Core, and content namespaces are explicit; hostile local-name collisions are rejected or ignored.
Exactly maxFeedBytes is accepted and max+1 is rejected while all fetches remain bounded by the shared fetcher.
Independent reviewer approved exact revision aac1e87f5714ca256c35e978ab49a74debc5ea2e after transactional, namespace, and boundary corrections.

notes: No direct HTTP client, HTML fallback, or permission bypass was introduced.
